headline: 英國藝術資助80週年
context: 英國文化圈這邊，藝術協會英格蘭（Arts Council England）迎來成立80週年，前Channel 5台長道恩．艾雷（Dawn Airey）本週接任主席一職。同時，《衛報》影評也介紹了兩部新片：改編自朵薇．楊笙小說的《夏日之書》，以及以模里西斯殖民時代為背景的《天堂囚徒》。

sources.name: The Guardian
sources.summary: This sensitive adaptation of Jansson’s 1972 novel, set in the beatific Gulf of Finland, is a quiet treatise on life and death Glenn Close brings her totemic presence to this gentle movie – as well as a makeup-enhanced grandmotherly face. This is a sweet-natured adaptation of Tove Jansson’s 1972 novel; it has charm, though it’s sometimes becalmed in its own sensitivity. Close plays a tough, wise, humorous-yet-cantankerous eightysomething woman who likes cigarettes and walking around outside stark naked when there’s nobody else around. She brings her recently widowed son (Anders Danielsen Lie) and six-year-old granddaughter Sophia (newcomer Emily Matthews) to a tiny, idyllic island in the Gulf of Finland, where they have a summer cottage. The grandmother may, incidentally, have unresolved feelings for local man Eriksson, in a fleeting cameo for veteran Icelandic actor Ingvar Sigurdsson. Continue reading...
sources.title: The Summer Book review – Glenn Close powers sweet-natured take on Tove Jansson’s grief classic

sources.name: The Guardian
sources.summary: An upper-class Englishwoman falls in love with a worker on her uncle’s sugar plantation in this insipid adaptation of Romesh Gunesekera’s novel Here is a tale of love across the divide, based on a novel by Booker nominee Romesh Gunesekera . Set in 1925, it revolves around 17-year-old Lucy (Ellie Bamber), a beautiful young upper-class Englishwoman sent to live on her uncle’s sugar plantation in colonial Mauritius. There she meets Krishna (Mehdi Dehbi), a local man of Indian heritage employed by her uncle in the fields. In a Mr Darcy-style moment early on, Lucy spies Krishna stripped to the waist and splashing about in a waterfall. But Prisoners of Paradise is a chaste and idealistic drama, and even this moment is filmed in a damp, unerotic way, as if a bit of phwoar would sully Lucy and Krishna’s noble hearts. Lucy has arrived at Ambleside, the plantation house owned by her uncle George (Rupert Penry-Jones) after the death of her mother. Mauritius’s economy was built on the labour of African slaves and later indentured workers from India. It’s now nearly a century after the abolition of slavery, but uncle George has not removed the torture instruments from his garden, where shackles still hang from a post. He also clings to abhorrent beliefs about racial superiority. Lucy is appalled by his views, and shocked by the casual racism in his circle. When she falls for Krishna, they begin to meet in secret. sources.name: The Guardian
sources.summary: Arts Council England has been much criticised in recent years. A new chair offers hope for a weary cultural sector “I do not believe it is yet realised what an important thing has happened,” the economist John Maynard Keynes wrote in The Listener in July 1945 . “Patronage of the arts has crept in. It has happened in a very English, informal, unostentatious way – half baked if you like.” He was referring to the wartime Council for the Encouragement of Music and the Arts (Cema), which would become the Arts Council of Great Britain. Keynes died a few months before it was granted a royal charter on 9 August 1946. A body to secure and distribute government cultural investment was created – an important thing, indeed. The Arts Council initially funded 46 institutions , including the Royal Opera House and Bristol Old Vic , the first publicly funded regional theatre in the UK. Over eight decades it has contributed to the making of world-renowned treasures such as the Southbank Centre and Royal Shakespeare Company. Today it supports nearly 1,000 organisations from the Proms to Glastonbury, local libraries, comedy venues and community arts centres, as well as individual artists. In 1994 it was devolved into national councils. This week Dawn Airey , the former head of Channel 5, took over as chair of Arts Council England (ACE) from Sir Nicholas Serota. thread_text:
英國文化圈這邊，藝術協會英格蘭（Arts Council England）迎來成立80週年，前Channel 5台長道恩．艾雷（Dawn Airey）本週接任主席一職，外界期待她為疲軟的文化圈注入新氣象。同一天的影評版，《衛報》也介紹了兩部新片——改編自朵薇．楊笙（Tove Jansson）小說的《夏日之書》，由葛倫．克蘿絲（Glenn Close）主演；以及以20世紀初模里西斯殖民時代為背景的《天堂囚徒》。

—— 本則整理自 The Guardian 的報導，讓圖書館員翻譯給你聽。
threads_text:
英國文化圈這邊，藝術協會英格蘭（Arts Council England）迎來成立80週年。經濟學家凱因斯（John Maynard Keynes）在1945年促成了這個機構的前身，如今它已支持將近1,000個藝術組織，從逍遙音樂節（the Proms）到地方圖書館都在資助範圍內。這週，前Channel 5台長道恩．艾雷（Dawn Airey）接任主席，外界期待她為近年屢遭批評的協會帶來新氣象。另一則來自影評版，《衛報》介紹了兩部新片：改編自芬蘭作家朵薇．楊笙（Tove Jansson）小說的《夏日之書》，由葛倫．克蘿絲（Glenn Close）主演，講一位老奶奶與孫女在芬蘭灣小島上的夏天；還有以1925年模里西斯殖民時代為背景的《天堂囚徒》，講一段跨越階級與種族的禁忌戀情。

本則整理自 The Guardian 於 2026 年 8 月 4 日至 5 日發佈的報導。
voice_text: 英國的藝術協會英格蘭，今年滿80週年了。這個機構最早由經濟學家凱因斯促成，如今支持將近1,000個藝術組織，從音樂節到地方圖書館都在資助範圍內。這星期，前電視台台長道恩．艾雷接任主席，外界期待她為近年屢遭批評的協會帶來新氣象。影劇這邊也有兩部新片。《夏日之書》改編自芬蘭作家朵薇．楊笙的小說，葛倫．克蘿絲演一位老奶奶，陪孫女在芬蘭灣的小島上度過一個夏天。另一部《天堂囚徒》，背景設在1925年的模里西斯，講一段跨越階級與種族的禁忌戀情。
